html:
The Bularnu were an Aboriginal Australian people of the dry country on the border of Queensland and the Northern Territory, around the upper Georgina River.

Very little is recorded about them, and the name refers above all to their language, now no longer spoken. Their neighbours on the map are the Warluwarra, Wakaya, Andegerebenha and Kalkadoon. Cattle stations spread along the Georgina in the 1870s and 1880s.
sum: The Bularnu were an Aboriginal Australian people of the dry country on the border of Queensland and the Northern Territory, around the upper Georgina River.
